zone-intro:1.text: The new template built for this slot was not intuitive — it was complicated to follow. A viewer could not tell at a glance what it was showing: the source tile, the two rails, the travelling clones and the condition chips all had to be pieced together before the point landed. The lesson is about legibility, not about card count or about whether to commission cards: a newly built template has to read INSTANTLY, on one viewing, with no audio. If it needs the viewer to work out how to read it, it fails regardless of how well it maps to the clause. Proposing a new card stays a first-class outcome; this particular one was not followable.
zone-intro:1.resolution: card-library/DESIGN.md — new-card checklist item 7 now requires the mute test answered FROM A RENDERED FRAME, and a new section explains that lint/card-qa/check-type-scale all pass on a card nobody can follow. Deliberately NOT routed to the zone rulebook: the lesson is about how a card is BUILT, and the body pass proposes cards too, so the zone rulebook would have hidden it from half the pipeline.

_global:player.text: Could not play the video on the per-cue player — it showed 0:00 / 0:00. Root cause: the board serves per-cue audio from videos/<slug>/slices/<cueId>.mp3 and builds those at boot only when resolved.json is present. Gate 1 (037) has to be reviewed BEFORE 040 exists, so the board was started without resolved.json, booted in card-plan-only mode, and never sliced. Restarting after 040 produced all 39 slices. Nothing was wrong with the player; it was rendering a dead <audio> element with no way to say so.
_global:player.resolution: No rule change. Instance cause: the board was started before resolved.json existed (Gate 1 requires it pre-040), so it booted in card-plan-only mode and never built slices. Restarting after 040 produced all 39. Noted here so the next session recognises 0:00/0:00 as "restart the board", not a broken player.

_global:logo-on-every-graphic.text: Standing preference: every motion graphic should carry a colour logo, image or icon — not text alone. Raised against enacted/spotlight-focus, which named OpusClip and Submagic as bare text with no marks. Survey: 39 of 52 fullframe cards in the catalog are text-only; only 13 accept a logo slug.
_global:logo-on-every-graphic.resolution: card-library/DESIGN.md — new section "A graphic carries a mark, not text alone" plus checklist item 6. Templates changed: enacted/spotlight-focus and enacted/race-bars now accept productLogos[] (index-aligned, a shape logos-inline.mjs already inlines) and render the colour mark; z11/z12 cues updated and verified through the render path. Remaining debt recorded in DESIGN.md: 39 of 52 fullframe cards are text-only, which is a sweep, but no NEW card may be added text-only.

_global:cta-copy-constant.text: pls dont make link in descirption, subscribe related teampltes - text dynamic. lets keep it constant and simple..
_global:cta-copy-constant.resolution: The ask is identical in every video, so a per-cue text variable bought nothing and invited drift between cues (this video had 'Both tools linked in the description' on one cue and 'Link in description' on another). Copy is now baked into all three CTA cards: link-scrim 'Links in the description', link-in-description 'Link in description', like-subscribe 'Subscribe'. Machine-enforced rather than prose: all three catalog entries now declare variables:{} so the resolver rejects any authored copy. link-scrim's `kicker` was a second authored line and its element, CSS, render lines and tween were removed rather than left as an unreachable branch. Misleading '--variables' override comments in the card headers corrected. R_LINK_CTA in lib/cue-rules.mjs now states CTA cards carry NO variables, and cue-pass-prompt.md regenerated so the pass actually sees it.

_global:overflow-not-gated.text: why was this overflow issue not fixed. this card looks bad. more than fix - i want rca why this was not auotmaltically fixed and hiw to avoid this long term
_global:overflow-not-gated.resolution: RCA, three independent gaps — the defect needed all three. (1) THE PROBE IS A BADGE, NOT A GATE. The overflow measurement lives entirely inside board.mjs as client-side JS in the preview iframe (measures against W=1920 H=1080 TOL=2, posts __overflow, paints a red badge). Grepped for consumers: none. So the pipeline DETECTS the clipping and ships it anyway; it is caught only if a human happens to look at that tile. Same shape decisions.md logs four times on 2026-07-25: computed on one surface, never consumed on the next. (2) card-qa TESTS THE CARD, NEVER THE CUE. It renders each card's own min/max variants from declared capacity — synthetic content. It never saw title='Submagic: Straight To Posted' with a 3-node vertical chain, so the card was certified 'no clipping at max' while the real cue overflowed. (3) THE VARIANT ROTATION MOVED THE GOALPOSTS AFTER THE COPY WAS WRITTEN. resolve.mjs:361 rotates variants by use count; pipeline-flow is used 3x so c17 got variant b (vertical, least vertical headroom) while z05/c19 stayed on a. The cue pass wrote a 4-word title against a's horizontal layout, the resolver silently swapped the layout, and nothing re-checked fit. `title` had no max_words at all, so no cap could reject it. FIXED: catalog now caps pipeline-flow title at max_words 3 (variant b's real limit) — proven to bite, it rejected all three existing titles at 040 before I shortened them; titles are now 'Both Tools Promise' / 'Straight To Posted' / 'The Cleanup Lap', frame-verified at 1920x1080 in variant b. DESIGN.md gains 'Declared capacity is the TIGHTEST variant's capacity'. STILL OPEN (architectural, needs a plan not an inline hack): promote the board's overflow probe into a headless per-cue gate that runs against resolved.json at each beat time and fails 040/090. The measurement is DOM-based so it needs a browser, but card-qa already renders headlessly, so the machinery exists. Until that lands, overflow on REAL cue content is caught by eye only.

z03.text: why speed first is not highliighted in orange?

context.anchor: By the end of this video

z03.resolution: Answered: the card only ever gave orange to a winner defaulting to the LAST option, and it ignored authored beats entirely. Fixed the card: promise-payoff now consumes variables.beats and, with no winner set, lights EVERY resolved option in accent — a question card must not pre-answer itself. Durable: new E12 lint fails resolve when a beat reveal names an option/item the card never declared (z03s old beats did exactly that, silently). Frame-verified: both plates orange with checks.

z05.text: why from 05 to 017, screen is static with no motion. i thought we fixed such issues permanently. also pink color doesn't suit
z05.resolution: Two causes. Static screen: the ambient rule allowed a 1.2% breathe that is imperceptible over a 17s hold — DESIGN.md gains the long-hold tier (holds >8s need a VISIBLE loop) and pipeline-flow now carries a travelling track sheen; new W20 lint warns when a cue holds a card past 2x its designed duration. Pink: --negative rose #fb7185 swept out of all 16 cards. Owner refined the replacement live on the board: connecting lines stay ORANGE (gold read as stray yellow) and no red fail-finale — every node resolves orange with a check; red survives only as static no-marks. Frame-verified on The Cleanup Lap.

c20.text: Can we make better rule on when to use this motion graphic template. I dont think for this big of a text, we should have used this template. Also why everyhting is small. THis template is more imp sections, small letter looks very bad..

context.anchor: once you factor in the extra editing time

c20.resolution: Your rule, written: R_KINETIC now carries the STATEMENT TEST — kinetic type carries a declarative statement that could stand alone as a pull-quote, never instructions or on-screen actions — plus a word cap cut 18->12 with the core-clause escape hatch. The card sizes by length bucket (<=8 words 120px, 9-12 96px) so a statement LOOKS like one. c20 re-authored to the verbatim core clause. Bonus find while frame-verifying: the renderer drops var(--accent) colors on these spans in --variables renders (fine in browser/board) — every past kinetic render shipped white accents; card now resolves the token and inlines the literal. Frame-verified orange.

c17.resolution: Instance fix: re-cued from enacted/pipeline-flow (3rd use in this video, and the moment is a pulling-ahead, not a pipeline) to enacted/race-bars with product logos — Submagic 100 vs OpusClip 65 on the final beat. Pink handled globally per z05. Frame-verified.

c04.text: in all of my templates, text size looks off. Like heading is very big, rest all are very small. Can we fix this. For context - previous we might have added some rule for text size. tell me what can we do to make it better.
c04.resolution: The rule you remembered (hero 120-200px, minimum 2.5x ratio) had no ceiling and no body floor — pros-cons was COMPLIANT at 150px over 28px rows (5.4x). DESIGN.md now caps hero at 4x the row text and floors fullframe rows at 36px; check-type-scale.mjs enforces both (it caught and fixed two more library cards). pros-cons is now 128px hero over 38px rows. Frame-verified with the real Submagic content.

z08.text: why orange boundary is not complete.. looks weird

context.anchor: you will find the links in the description

z08.resolution: The border was a 1px stroke at 0.42 alpha — a hairline that partially vanishes through encode and reads as a broken ring. DESIGN.md rule: any stroke meant to read as a complete shape is >=2px at >=0.6 alpha. link-scrim border is now 2.5px at 0.75. Frame-verified: complete ring.

z01.resolution: Redone per your direction C: new card statement/strike-list — the statement holds the frame, Captions/Pacing/Layouts (with concept icons) are struck out in red one per beat, and Badly takes the accent sweep on the final strike. _chat:orange-only-chain.resolution: Applied over the batch-approved gold-sweep+red-fail split after seeing it rendered: pipeline-flow track fills stay accent orange in every register, the red fail-finale (red node + X badge + judder) is removed — every node resolves orange with a check. DESIGN.md and EDITOR-STYLE-GUIDE.md palette rules updated to match: red is only ever a static no-mark, never motion or a chain state; gold stays winner-only.
